data.name: Karthik
data.gender_notes: Karthik is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Karthik is a Sanskrit name derived from the Hindu deity Lord Karthikeya. He is considered the god of agriculture, fertility, and war. He is also known as the lord of virtues and wisdom. The name Karthik carries the meaning “God of Agriculture” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Karthik usually hope their child will grow to embody god of agriculture and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Karthik belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Agriculture.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Karthik total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Karthik carries immense religious and cultural significance for the Hindu community. It evokes images of Lord Karthikeya, the son of Shiva and Parvathi, who is considered the lord of art, music, beauty, and love. Naming a child Karthik is a way of connecting the child to this eternal deity, reinforcing the rich Hindu heritage and tradition. This name is popularly used among families who value their Hindu heritage and seek to instill the virtues and values associated with Lord Karthikeya in their children.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Karthik lies in its association with the god Lord Karthikeya. In Hindu mythology, Lord Karthikeya is considered the god of wisdom, virtue, and knowledge. By naming a child Karthik, parents are bestowing upon them the blessings of this deity, hoping that their child will grow up to be wise, virtuous, and knowledgeable. This name serves as a daily reminder of the importance of living a virtuous and spiritual life, imbuing the child with a strong moral compass and a deep sense of spirituality.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Karthik: The radiant moon, illuminating the path to knowledge and wisdom. A name that symbolizes enlightenment and inner peace.

vedic_reference.note: The name Karthikeya is mentioned in various Hindu texts, including the Skanda Purana.

historical_references.context: An epic Sanskrit poem that forms a major source for Hindu mythology and Indian philosophies, especially Jainism and Buddhism.

historical_references.reference: Karthikayani, a goddess revered in South India, especially in Tamil Nadu, believed to be the embodiment of the god Shiva's wife Parvati during her menstrual period.
historical_references.context: Hindu goddess worshipped during the festivals of Karthikai and Kartik Purnima, which falls around November in the Gregorian calendar.
